stimulus.body: A: 会议改到周五。 B: 周五？ A: 对，周五上午。 B: 收到。

questions.stem: What did Speaker B do?

options.text: Changed the meeting to Friday
Echoed the day to confirm
Cancelled the meeting
Ignored Speaker A

questions.explanation: Speaker B echoed '周五' to confirm, then said '收到'; the distractors misread the intent.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: Choose the phrase that interrupts to share urgent info
questions.stem: You have urgent information to share mid-discussion; which Chinese phrase interrupts politely?

options.text: 我有急事 (I have something urgent)
紧急情况 (Urgent situation)
等一下 (Wait)

questions.explanation: '不好意思' plus the urgent notice politely signals the interruption; the distractors are abrupt or ignore turn-taking.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: Explain how to agree to review something in Chinese
questions.stem: You agree to review a document but not to approve it yet; write a natural Chinese sentence.

answer.exemplar: 我可以先看看，但不一定能通过。 (I can take a look first, but I can't guarantee approval.)

questions.explanation: Agreeing to review while withholding approval keeps commitment measured; it sets clear expectations.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a short dialogue and identify the disagreement strategy

stimulus.body: A: 我们应该先做功能X。 B: 功能X很重要，但用户反馈显示功能Y更紧急。 A: 那先做Y吧。

questions.stem: How did Speaker B disagree?

options.text: By rejecting X as useless
By acknowledging X's importance then citing user feedback for Y
By fully agreeing to do X first
By changing the subject

questions.explanation: Speaker B acknowledged X's importance and then cited user feedback prioritizing Y; the distractors misread tone or intent.
